title: Pistachio Tahini Halva Squares
summary: Fudgy tahini halva made by beating hot sugar syrup into sesame paste, studded with pistachios and pressed into a tin to set.
equipment: stand mixer with paddle, or a large bowl and sturdy spatula

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Line the tin
steps.text: Line the tin with baking paper, leaving extra hanging over two sides so you can lift the halva out later.

steps.title: Prepare the tahini
steps.text: Put the tahini, salt and vanilla in the mixer bowl and fold in the chopped pistachios.

steps.title: Cook the syrup
steps.text: Put the sugar, water and lemon zest in the saucepan over medium heat and stir until the sugar dissolves. Then simmer without stirring for 6-8 min, until the thermometer reads 118 °C.

steps.title: Beat together briefly
steps.text: Run the mixer on medium-low and pour the hot syrup into the tahini in a thin stream. Mix for just 30-60 seconds, until the mixture thickens and starts to pull away from the sides of the bowl.

steps.title: Press into the tin
steps.text: Scrape it into the tin straight away, lay a sheet of baking paper on top and press it flat and even with your hands.

steps.title: Cool and cut
steps.text: Leave to cool to room temperature for about 2 h, until firm. Lift it out and cut into 16 squares.

tips: The most common mistake is overmixing; beating too long turns the halva sandy and crumbly, so stop as soon as it pulls away from the bowl.
Stir the tahini thoroughly before measuring, as the oil separates in the jar.
Use a light, runny tahini made from hulled seeds for the palest colour and mildest flavour.
Add 0.5 tsp ground cardamom to the tahini for a fragrant variation.
storage: Wrap well and keep at room temperature for up to 2 weeks or in the fridge for up to 1 month.
